safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 5.0 to 2.11 days

narrative: Material PL1__M155CAF3 exhibits smooth, high-frequency demand (CV=0.387) with a mild decreasing trend over the observation window. Lead times average 2.61 days but show high variability (CV=0.429), which drives the safety stock requirement. The EOQ-based (r,Q) policy is selected because smooth demand with near-100% non-zero fraction and a high ordering cost relative to unit holding cost strongly favours large, infrequent replenishment batches. Increasing the order quantity from 1,002 to 8,897 units reduces annual total costs by 75.8% while maintaining the 95% service level target.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand pattern (CV=0.387, 100% non-zero fraction) with a high fixed ordering cost (75 USD) relative to per-unit holding cost (0.234 USD/unit/yr) makes the classical EOQ-driven (r,Q) policy optimal. The policy minimises total annual cost while meeting the 95% service level via the combined demand-and-lead-time sigma formula.
research_insights.boundary_risk: EOQ order quantity (8,897) + safety stock (1,044) = 9,941 units, which is 39.6% of the 25,080-unit storage capacity. No capacity constraint binds. However, the detected decreasing demand trend may reduce annual demand and shift the EOQ downward over time.
